# Amani Restaurant Website
## Vite + React Production Architecture, Security, SEO and Development Playbook

**Architecture type:** Static React website generated by Vite  
**Hosting target:** GoDaddy Linux Web Hosting / cPanel  
**Deployment output:** Upload the contents of `dist/` to `public_html/`  
**Last reviewed:** 6 August 2026  
**Primary goal:** A minimal, luxurious, fast and accessible restaurant website with refined Awwwards-level motion, without requiring a Node.js server or complex backend infrastructure.

---

## 1. Final Technical Decision

Use a **single Vite + React + TypeScript application** that builds into static HTML, CSS, JavaScript and media files.

The website will use:

- React for UI components and page composition
- Vite for local development and production builds
- TypeScript for safer code and easier maintenance
- React Router for the five public pages
- Tailwind CSS for utility styling and design tokens
- Motion for React for component entrances, hover states and layout transitions
- GSAP with ScrollTrigger only for complex cinematic sequences
- Lenis for one global smooth-scroll system
- Lucide React for interface icons
- Local TypeScript data files for menu, reviews, opening hours and restaurant information
- A small optional PHP endpoint or a trusted external form service for enquiry submissions
- Apache `.htaccess` for React route fallback, HTTPS, caching and security headers

### Why this architecture fits GoDaddy

Vite produces a static `dist/` folder. GoDaddy cPanel hosting can serve these files directly from `public_html`, so the production server does not need Node.js, npm or a running React process.

### Explicitly excluded from the first version

Do not add these unless the business later requires them:

- Next.js
- Payload CMS
- Node.js production server
- Express
- Separate backend repository
- PostgreSQL or MongoDB
- Docker
- Redux
- GraphQL
- WebSockets
- Three.js or WebGL merely for decoration
- Multiple smooth-scroll libraries
- Multiple animation libraries controlling the same element

This limitation keeps the site affordable, stable and easy to deploy.

## 2. Site Map and Route Architecture

| Route | Page | Main sections |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | Home | Hero, Brand Introduction, Mood Finder, Signature Experiences, Signature Dishes, The Amani Way, Inside Amani, Guest Reviews, Visit Preview, Gatherings Preview, Final Reservation Invitation, Footer |
| `/stories/` | Stories | Hero, Why Amani, Our Beginning, The Philosophy, From Kitchen to Table, Our People, A Day at Amani, Closing Invitation |
| `/menu/` | Menu | Hero, Practical Menu Introduction, Sticky Categories, Mood Finder, Menu Categories, Dish Detail Experience, Dietary and Service Information, QR Ordering Information, Closing Gallery / Reservation Invitation |
| `/gatherings/` | Gatherings | Hero, Gatherings Introduction, Occasions, Spaces and Formats, Gallery, Planning Process, Enquiry Form, Closing Statement |
| `/visit/` | Visit | Hero, Live Status, Location and Directions, Restaurant Information, Contact, FAQs, Menu / Reservation Invitation |
| `*` | Not Found | Helpful 404 page with links to Home, Menu and Visit |

### Shared website shell

Every page must use the same shell:

1. Skip-to-content link
2. Utility bar
3. Header/navigation
4. Main page content
5. Footer
6. Reservation CTA
7. Optional mobile sticky action bar
8. Route-change focus and scroll restoration

### Header navigation

- Logo → `/`
- Menu → `/menu/`
- Stories → `/stories/`
- Gatherings → `/gatherings/`
- Visit → `/visit/`
- Reserve a Table → configured external booking URL, phone, WhatsApp or enquiry anchor

### Utility bar

- Live open/closed status
- Today’s closing time
- Serving area or neighbourhood
- Get Directions link

The utility bar must not contain information duplicated unnecessarily in the main navigation.

## 3. Recommended Stack

### Runtime dependencies

```bash
npm install react react-dom react-router-dom
npm install motion gsap @gsap/react lenis
npm install lucide-react
npm install clsx tailwind-merge
npm install zod
npm install @unhead/react
```

### Development dependencies

```bash
npm install -D vite typescript @vitejs/plugin-react
npm install -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
npm install -D eslint prettier
npm install -D vitest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom jsdom
npm install -D playwright
```

### Dependency responsibilities

| Package | Responsibility | Do not use it for |
|---|---|---|
| React | Component composition and state | Direct DOM animation |
| React Router | Pages, links, 404 and route lazy-loading | Server-side rendering |
| Tailwind CSS | Layout, spacing, typography and responsive styling | Complex animation timelines |
| Motion for React | Entrances, hover, tap, presence and layout motion | Large pinned scroll narratives |
| GSAP | Coordinated timelines and exact animation choreography | Every small hover effect |
| ScrollTrigger | Complex scroll-linked sequences | Ordinary fade-up sections |
| Lenis | Global smooth scrolling | Page transitions or element animation |
| Lucide | Consistent icons | Brand logo or decorative illustrations |
| Zod | Client-side form schema validation | Security validation on the server |
| Unhead | Page title, metadata, canonical and social tags | Replacing prerendering |
| Vitest | Unit and component testing | Browser-level journeys |
| Playwright | Critical user-flow testing and optional prerender scripts | Unit testing |

### Version policy

- Install current stable releases.
- Commit `package-lock.json`.
- Do not use unpinned CDN scripts in production.
- Review major version upgrades separately.
- Run `npm audit` and manually assess the actual production risk before updating blindly.

### Folder rules

- Pages assemble sections but contain little detailed UI code.
- Each section has one clear purpose and its own folder when complex.
- Shared components must be genuinely reusable.
- Content must not be buried inside animation code.
- Configuration values belong in `src/config`.
- Restaurant copy and menu data belong in `src/content`.
- No component file should become a page-sized monolith.
- Avoid barrel exports when they hide circular dependencies.

## 5. Application Bootstrap

### `src/main.tsx`

```tsx
import React from "react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";
import "./styles/globals.css";
import "lenis/dist/lenis.css";
import { AppProviders } from "./app/providers";
import { App } from "./app/App";

const root = document.getElementById("root");

if (!root) {
  throw new Error("Root element was not found");
}

ReactDOM.createRoot(root).render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <AppProviders>
      <App />
    </AppProviders>
  </React.StrictMode>,
);
```

### `src/app/App.tsx`

```tsx
import { RouterProvider } from "react-router-dom";
import { router } from "./router";

export function App() {
  return <RouterProvider router={router} />;
}
```

### `src/app/router.tsx`

Use lazy route modules so users do not download every page immediately.

```tsx
import { createBrowserRouter } from "react-router-dom";
import { PublicLayout } from "../layouts/PublicLayout";
import { RouteErrorBoundary } from "./RouteErrorBoundary";

export const router = createBrowserRouter([
  {
    path: "/",
    element: <PublicLayout />,
    errorElement: <RouteErrorBoundary />,
    children: [
      {
        index: true,
        lazy: () => import("../pages/home/route"),
      },
      {
        path: "stories",
        lazy: () => import("../pages/stories/route"),
      },
      {
        path: "menu",
        lazy: () => import("../pages/menu/route"),
      },
      {
        path: "gatherings",
        lazy: () => import("../pages/gatherings/route"),
      },
      {
        path: "visit",
        lazy: () => import("../pages/visit/route"),
      },
      {
        path: "*",
        lazy: () => import("../pages/not-found/route"),
      },
    ],
  },
]);
```

### Example route module

```tsx
import { HomePage } from "./HomePage";

export function Component() {
  return <HomePage />;
}
```

## 6. Provider Architecture

Use only the providers that are necessary.

```tsx
import type { PropsWithChildren } from "react";
import { MotionConfig } from "motion/react";
import { createHead, UnheadProvider } from "@unhead/react/client";
import { SmoothScrollProvider } from "../components/motion/SmoothScrollProvider";

const head = createHead();

export function AppProviders({ children }: PropsWithChildren) {
  return (
    <UnheadProvider head={head}>
      <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">
        <SmoothScrollProvider>{children}</SmoothScrollProvider>
      </MotionConfig>
    </UnheadProvider>
  );
}
```

### Provider rules

- Only one Lenis instance for the entire application.
- Register GSAP plugins once.
- Do not wrap every section in a new context provider.
- Do not add global state unless multiple distant sections genuinely share changing data.
- Static restaurant data should be imported, not stored in React context.

## 7. Design System for a Minimal Luxury Restaurant

The visual character should feel editorial, warm, composed and tactile.

### Recommended visual principles

- Large photography with deliberate cropping
- Calm spacing and strong whitespace
- Restrained type scale
- One serif display family plus one clean sans-serif family
- Fine lines rather than heavy borders
- Soft contrast rather than pure black everywhere
- Buttons that feel tactile but not playful
- Minimal card containers
- Natural texture used as an accent, not a noisy background
- One primary call to action per section

### Avoid

- Generic SaaS card grids
- Bright neon gradients
- Excessive glassmorphism
- Numerous pills and badges
- Large shadows on every element
- Random floating decorative shapes
- Excessive rounded corners
- Animating every line of copy
- Long sections created only to support scroll effects

### Design token system: `src/styles/tokens.css`

All tokens use the `--amani-*` prefix. This is the single source of truth. Do not introduce any other prefix or naming convention.

```css
:root {
  /* Primary canvases */
  --amani-canvas:        #F8F2E5;
  --amani-paper:         #EFE5D4;
  --amani-sand:          #D8C7AA;

  /* Typography */
  --amani-ink:           #171411;
  --amani-ink-soft:      #403A34;
  --amani-muted:         #746E66;

  /* Brand accents */
  --amani-wine:          #7A1F24;
  --amani-wine-deep:     #551317;
  --amani-rust:          #A2553E;
  --amani-olive:         #6D7254;

  /* Structure */
  --amani-line:          rgba(23, 20, 17, 0.16);
  --amani-line-strong:   rgba(23, 20, 17, 0.34);
  --amani-overlay:       rgba(15, 12, 10, 0.34);

  /* Dark scenes */
  --amani-night:         #11100E;
  --amani-night-soft:    #1B1814;
  --amani-light-on-dark: #F4EDDF;

  /* Feedback states */
  --amani-success:       #315a3f;
  --amani-error:         #8a2f28;

  /* Typography families */
  --amani-font-display: "Cormorant Garamond", Georgia, serif;
  --amani-font-ui:      "Manrope", Arial, sans-serif;

  /* Fluid type scale */
  --amani-type-hero:        clamp(4rem,   9.4vw, 10.5rem);
  --amani-type-display-xl:  clamp(3.5rem, 7vw,    7.5rem);
  --amani-type-display-lg:  clamp(2.8rem, 5.4vw,  5.8rem);
  --amani-type-display-md:  clamp(2.15rem,3.7vw,  4rem);
  --amani-type-title:       clamp(1.65rem,2.3vw,  2.6rem);
  --amani-type-body-lg:     clamp(1.08rem,1.35vw, 1.35rem);
  --amani-type-body:        1rem;
  --amani-type-label:       0.72rem;

  /* Spacing scale */
  --amani-space-1:  0.375rem;
  --amani-space-2:  0.75rem;
  --amani-space-3:  1.125rem;
  --amani-space-4:  1.5rem;
  --amani-space-5:  2rem;
  --amani-space-6:  3rem;
  --amani-space-7:  4.5rem;
  --amani-space-8:  6rem;
  --amani-space-9:  8rem;
  --amani-space-10: 11rem;

  /* Layout */
  --amani-section-block-desktop: clamp(6rem,  11vw, 11rem);
  --amani-section-block-mobile:  clamp(4rem,  18vw,  6.5rem);
  --amani-gutter:                clamp(1rem,   3vw,   3.5rem);
  --amani-container:             1600px;
  --amani-reading-width:         66ch;

  /* Border radius */
  --amani-radius-none: 0;

  /* Shadow */

  --amani-ease-luxury: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);
  --amani-duration-fast: 350ms;
  --amani-duration-base: 600ms;
  --amani-duration-slow: 920ms;

```

### Typography requirements

- The page title must be one visible `<h1>`.
- Section titles should normally be `<h2>`.
- Do not skip heading levels for visual styling.
- Keep paragraph line length near 58–68 characters (`--amani-reading-width: 66ch`).
- Use `clamp()` for fluid display sizes (see `--amani-type-*` tokens).
- Display/emotional headings: `--amani-font-display` (Cormorant Garamond Variable).
- Body/UI/labels: `--amani-font-ui` (Manrope Variable).
- Load only required font weights.
- Self-host properly licensed font files where possible.
- Preload only the most important above-the-fold font file.

## 8. Motion Architecture

Awwwards-level work does not mean adding maximum animation. It means using timing, hierarchy, continuity and restraint to support the restaurant story.

### Animation ownership rule

Each animation must have one owner.

| Need | Owner |
|---|---|
| Basic colour, underline or small transform transition | CSS |
| Button hover, card hover, modal, mobile menu, layout and entrance | Motion for React |
| Multi-element hero timeline or complex reveal choreography | GSAP |
| Pinned narrative, image expansion or horizontal gallery | GSAP ScrollTrigger |
| Smooth document scrolling | Lenis |

**Never allow Motion and GSAP to animate the same property on the same element.**

### Global motion limits

All motion values must be sourced from `src/lib/motionTokens.ts`. Do not use arbitrary values.

- Use one signature animation per major section.
- Supporting motion must remain subtle.
- Typical reveal distance: `16px` to `32px` (`motionTokens.distance.sm` to `motionTokens.distance.lg`).
- Typical section reveal duration: `0.5s` to `0.8s` (use `motionTokens.duration.base`).
- Typical stagger: `0.05s` to `0.1s` (`motionTokens.stagger.tight` to `motionTokens.stagger.base`).
- Hover lift: no more than `4px` (`motionTokens.cardHoverLift`).
- Image hover scale: no more than `1.035` (`motionTokens.imageHoverScale`).
- Press scale: `0.985` minimum (`motionTokens.pressScale`).
- Avoid bounce unless the interaction specifically requires physical feedback.
- Avoid long forced loading screens.

### Recommended effects by section

#### Shared header

- Utility bar fades in once.
- Header logo and links enter with a restrained stagger.
- Header becomes more compact after scroll.
- On mobile, the menu uses `AnimatePresence` with proper focus handling.
- The Reserve CTA receives a minimal arrow or background-fill interaction.

#### Home Hero

- Use one coordinated GSAP entrance timeline.
- Reveal the hero media with a clip or mask.
- Reveal the eyebrow, heading, body and CTA in sequence.
- Optional subtle image scale from `1.04` to `1`.
- Do not pin the hero unless the concept clearly requires it.
- If using video, begin only when ready and never autoplay sound.

#### Mood Finder

- Use Motion layout transitions when the selected mood changes.
- Keep answers quick and understandable.
- Do not make content dependent on drag-only input.

#### Signature Experiences

- Editorial image-and-copy layout.
- A small parallax range can be used on desktop.
- Use ordinary stacking on mobile.

#### Signature Dishes

- Stagger cards only when first entering view.
- Image zoom may occur within an overflow-hidden frame.
- Dish details open in an accessible dialog or dedicated section.

#### The Amani Way

- Use a restrained story progression.
- Consider one sticky media panel on desktop only.
- Do not create multiple nested pins.

#### Inside Amani

- Use a gallery, editorial grid or horizontal drag interaction.
- On mobile, provide swipe and arrow controls.

#### Guest Reviews

- Keep motion secondary to readability.
- Auto-rotating carousels require pause controls.
- Prefer manual navigation.

#### Stories page

- Use long-form editorial rhythm.
- Image reveals and text transitions should be slow and composed.
- Avoid scroll hijacking.

#### Menu page

- Sticky category navigation should use native sticky positioning.
- Highlight the active category using lightweight state or Intersection Observer.
- Do not use ScrollTrigger simply to make the categories sticky.
- Dish details should be keyboard accessible.

#### Gatherings gallery

- Use an editorial image grid or one controlled horizontal sequence.
- Never hide required venue information behind animation.

#### Visit page

- Use minimal animation because users are performing practical tasks.
- Directions, hours, phone and reservation actions should remain immediately visible.

### Motion for React reveal component

```tsx
import type { PropsWithChildren } from "react";
import { motion, useReducedMotion } from "motion/react";
import { motionTokens } from "../../lib/motionTokens";

interface RevealProps extends PropsWithChildren {
  delay?: number;
  distance?: number;
  className?: string;
}

export function Reveal({ children, delay = 0, distance = motionTokens.distance.md, className }: RevealProps) {
  const shouldReduceMotion = useReducedMotion();

  return (
    <motion.div
      className={className}
      initial={shouldReduceMotion ? { opacity: 0 } : { opacity: 0, y: distance }}
      whileInView={shouldReduceMotion ? { opacity: 1 } : { opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
      viewport={{ once: true, amount: 0.25 }}
      transition={{
        duration: shouldReduceMotion ? 0.2 : motionTokens.duration.base,
        delay,
        ease: motionTokens.ease.standard,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}
```

### GSAP React cleanup pattern

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import gsap from "gsap";
import { useGSAP } from "@gsap/react";

export function Hero() {
  const root = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);

  useGSAP(
    () => {
      const timeline = gsap.timeline({ defaults: { ease: "power3.out" } });

      timeline
        .from("[data-hero-media]", { clipPath: "inset(100% 0 0 0)", duration: 1.1 })
        .from("[data-hero-copy] > *", {
          opacity: 0,
          y: 28,
          duration: 0.75,
          stagger: 0.08,
        }, "-=0.55");
    },
    { scope: root },
  );

  return <section ref={root}>{/* content */}</section>;
}
```

### ScrollTrigger rules

- Register `ScrollTrigger` once.
- Use `useGSAP` or `gsap.context()` for cleanup.
- Use `gsap.matchMedia()` to create different desktop and mobile behavior.
- Animate children inside a pinned element, not the pinned element itself.
- Refresh measurements after fonts and critical images are ready when necessary.
- Do not pin content on small mobile screens unless thoroughly tested.
- Every pinned sequence must have a reduced-motion static alternative.

### Lenis rules

- One global Lenis instance.
- Import the recommended Lenis CSS.
- Never initialize Lenis inside a page or section.
- Use native scroll on users who prefer reduced motion.
- Stop smooth scrolling while modal navigation is open when required.
- Ensure anchor links and keyboard scrolling still work.
- Synchronize Lenis and GSAP using one RAF/ticker integration only.

Because the first version has no CMS, use typed local data.

### `src/config/restaurant.ts`

```ts
export const restaurant = {
  name: "Amani",
  canonicalOrigin: "https://www.example.com",
  telephone: "+91XXXXXXXXXX",
  whatsappNumber: "91XXXXXXXXXX",
  email: "reservations@example.com",
  timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata",
  servesCuisine: ["Indian", "Contemporary"],
  priceRange: "₹₹₹",
  address: {
    streetAddress: "Replace with verified address",
    locality: "Replace with city",
    region: "Replace with state",
    postalCode: "Replace",
    country: "IN",
  },
  geo: {
    latitude: 0,
    longitude: 0,
  },
  directionsUrl: "https://maps.google.com/?q=REPLACE",
  reservationUrl: "https://example.com/reserve",
} as const;
```

### Menu data type

```ts
export interface Dish {
  id: string;
  slug: string;
  name: string;
  shortDescription: string;
  price: number;
  currency: "INR";
  categoryId: string;
  image: {
    src: string;
    alt: string;
    width: number;
    height: number;
  };
  dietary: Array<"vegetarian" | "vegan" | "contains-egg" | "non-vegetarian">;
  spiceLevel?: "mild" | "medium" | "hot";
  allergens?: string[];
  signature?: boolean;
  available?: boolean;
}
```

### Content rules

- Every record needs a stable ID or slug.
- Images require meaningful alt text or an empty alt for purely decorative images.
- Prices must be stored as numbers, not formatted strings.
- Availability should be clearly represented.
- Do not put critical menu information only inside an image or PDF.
- Keep opening hours in one configuration source.
- Avoid repeating business information separately across pages.

---

## 10. Live Open/Closed Status

The status must use the restaurant’s timezone, not the visitor’s device timezone.

```ts
interface OpeningWindow {
  opens: string;
  closes: string;
}

type WeeklyHours = Record<string, OpeningWindow[] | "closed">;

const weeklyHours: WeeklyHours = {
  monday: [{ opens: "12:00", closes: "23:00" }],
  tuesday: [{ opens: "12:00", closes: "23:00" }],
  wednesday: [{ opens: "12:00", closes: "23:00" }],
  thursday: [{ opens: "12:00", closes: "23:00" }],
  friday: [{ opens: "12:00", closes: "23:00" }],
  saturday: [{ opens: "12:00", closes: "23:00" }],
  sunday: [{ opens: "12:00", closes: "23:00" }],
};
```

### Requirements

- Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"`.
- Account for schedules that close after midnight.
- Keep holiday exceptions in a separate data object.
- Label calculated status as guidance when real-time kitchen/service status is unavailable.
- Do not claim “Open now” from stale hard-coded text.
- Give users the direct phone link to confirm on special dates.

---

## 11. SEO Architecture

A pure client-rendered SPA can be indexed, but initial HTML and social previews are more reliable when public routes are prerendered. For this five-page site, prerendering the final routes after `vite build` is strongly recommended.

### SEO implementation levels

#### Minimum launch level

- Unique title and description for every route
- Correct canonical URL
- Open Graph and social preview image
- Crawlable `<a href>` internal links
- `robots.txt`
- XML sitemap
- Restaurant JSON-LD
- Semantic HTML
- Readable menu text in the DOM
- Correct `lang` attribute
- Fast media and fonts

#### Recommended production level

- Prerender `/`, `/stories/`, `/menu/`, `/gatherings/` and `/visit/`
- Generate route-specific HTML at build time
- Test rendered HTML using Google Search Console URL Inspection
- Validate JSON-LD using Rich Results Test

### Page metadata plan

| Page | Suggested title direction | Search intent |
|---|---|---|
| Home | Amani — [Cuisine/Experience] Restaurant in [Area, City] | Brand and local discovery |
| Stories | Our Story — Amani Restaurant | Brand trust and philosophy |
| Menu | Menu — Amani Restaurant in [Area] | Menu and dining decision |
| Gatherings | Private Dining & Gatherings — Amani | Events and enquiries |
| Visit | Hours, Location & Reservations — Amani | Navigation and conversion |

Do not mechanically stuff location or cuisine keywords into every heading.

### SEO component example

```tsx
import { useHead } from "@unhead/react";

interface PageSeoProps {
  title: string;
  description: string;
  canonicalPath: string;
  image: string;
}

export function PageSeo({ title, description, canonicalPath, image }: PageSeoProps) {
  const origin = "https://www.example.com";
  const canonical = new URL(canonicalPath, origin).toString();
  const socialImage = new URL(image, origin).toString();

  useHead({
    title,
    meta: [
      { name: "description", content: description },
      { property: "og:type", content: "website" },
      { property: "og:title", content: title },
      { property: "og:description", content: description },
      { property: "og:url", content: canonical },
      { property: "og:image", content: socialImage },
      { name: "twitter:card", content: "summary_large_image" },
      { name: "twitter:title", content: title },
      { name: "twitter:description", content: description },
      { name: "twitter:image", content: socialImage },
    ],
    link: [{ rel: "canonical", href: canonical }],
  });

  return null;
}
```

### Restaurant JSON-LD example

Only publish verified information. Do not add ratings that are not visibly displayed and genuinely sourced.

```tsx
import { restaurant } from "../../config/restaurant";

export function RestaurantJsonLd() {
  const data = {
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "Restaurant",
    name: restaurant.name,
    url: restaurant.canonicalOrigin,
    image: [
      `${restaurant.canonicalOrigin}/og/home.jpg`,
    ],
    telephone: restaurant.telephone,
    email: restaurant.email,
    priceRange: restaurant.priceRange,
    servesCuisine: restaurant.servesCuisine,
    acceptsReservations: true,
    menu: `${restaurant.canonicalOrigin}/menu/`,
    address: {
      "@type": "PostalAddress",
      streetAddress: restaurant.address.streetAddress,
      addressLocality: restaurant.address.locality,
      addressRegion: restaurant.address.region,
      postalCode: restaurant.address.postalCode,
      addressCountry: restaurant.address.country,
    },
    geo: {
      "@type": "GeoCoordinates",
      latitude: restaurant.geo.latitude,
      longitude: restaurant.geo.longitude,
    },
  };

  return (
    <script
      type="application/ld+json"
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: JSON.stringify(data).replace(/</g, "\\u003c") }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Local SEO requirements

- Keep name, address and phone consistent across the site and Google Business Profile.
- Link “Get Directions” to the exact verified map listing.
- Include neighbourhood, city and cuisine naturally in visible copy.
- Display accurate opening hours.
- Add a direct phone link using `tel:`.
- Use a WhatsApp deep link only with the approved business number.
- Keep the menu accessible as HTML, even when a downloadable PDF is also supplied.
- Add descriptive internal links between Menu, Gatherings and Visit.
- Use real guest testimonials only with permission.
- Avoid fake urgency, fake scarcity and fake reviews.

### `public/robots.txt`

```txt
User-agent: *
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://www.example.com/sitemap.xml
```

### `public/sitemap.xml`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url><loc>https://www.example.com/</loc></url>
  <url><loc>https://www.example.com/stories/</loc></url>
  <url><loc>https://www.example.com/menu/</loc></url>
  <url><loc>https://www.example.com/gatherings/</loc></url>
  <url><loc>https://www.example.com/visit/</loc></url>
</urlset>
```

## 12. Security Model

The static Vite frontend has a small server attack surface, but it is not automatically secure.

### Non-negotiable rules

1. Never put private keys, SMTP passwords, admin credentials or secret API tokens in Vite code.
2. Any variable beginning with `VITE_` is visible to users after build.
3. Treat all browser input as untrusted.
4. Validate enquiry data again on the receiving server.
5. Do not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` for untrusted copy.
6. Do not store personal enquiry data in `localStorage`.
7. Use HTTPS everywhere.
8. Use trusted dependencies and commit the lockfile.
9. Restrict external scripts, embeds and domains.
10. Keep backups of the deployed site and source repository.

### Safe environment variables

```env
VITE_SITE_ORIGIN=https://www.example.com
VITE_MAPS_DIRECTIONS_URL=https://maps.google.com/?q=REPLACE
VITE_RESERVATION_URL=https://example.com/reserve
VITE_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_ID=
```

These must contain public configuration only.

### Unsafe environment variables

Never expose these as `VITE_*` values:

```text
SMTP_PASSWORD
DATABASE_PASSWORD
PRIVATE_API_KEY
ADMIN_TOKEN
RECAPTCHA_SECRET
TURNSTILE_SECRET
```

### Third-party script policy

- Add analytics only after consent requirements are understood.
- Load scripts with `defer` or asynchronously when supported.
- Do not install multiple analytics products at launch.
- Prefer a normal Maps link over an interactive map iframe when the iframe adds little value.
- If an iframe is used, lazy-load it and add a descriptive title.
- Restrict CSP to the exact domains actually required.

---

## 13. Secure Enquiry Form Options

A browser-only React application cannot securely send email using a private SMTP password.

Choose one of these approaches:

### Option A — External form provider

Use a reputable form provider that supports:

- server-side spam control
- origin/domain allowlisting
- rate limiting
- email delivery
- privacy terms
- minimal storage

This is the simplest choice.

### Option B — Minimal PHP endpoint on GoDaddy

Keep the React app static and add one small PHP endpoint under `/api/`.

Recommended location:

```text
public_html/
├── index.html
├── assets/
├── api/
│   └── gatherings-enquiry.php
└── .htaccess
```

### React form validation schema

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

export const enquirySchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().trim().min(2).max(80),
  email: z.string().trim().email().max(160),
  phone: z.string().trim().min(8).max(20),
  occasion: z.string().trim().min(2).max(80),
  eventDate: z.string().trim().max(20),
  guestCount: z.coerce.number().int().min(2).max(500),
  message: z.string().trim().max(1500),
  website: z.string().max(0), // honeypot field
});
```

Client-side validation improves UX but does not replace server validation.

### PHP endpoint security checklist

- Accept `POST` only.
- Require `application/json` or expected form encoding.
- Enforce a small request-body limit.
- Verify `Origin` or `Referer` against the production domain.
- Validate every field server-side.
- Reject the honeypot field when populated.
- Add rate limiting by IP or provider.
- Consider Cloudflare Turnstile for persistent spam.
- Do not permit file attachments.
- Do not reflect raw input into HTML.
- Escape any data inserted into HTML email.
- Prefer SMTP through an authenticated mail account.
- Log only operational metadata; avoid logging full private messages.
- Return generic errors to users.
- Keep PHP error display disabled in production.

### Simplified PHP outline

This is an outline, not a drop-in mail configuration. SMTP credentials must be stored outside public web files or in hosting environment/configuration.

```php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

header('Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8');
header('Cache-Control: no-store');

if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] !== 'POST') {
    http_response_code(405);
    echo json_encode(['ok' => false, 'message' => 'Method not allowed']);
    exit;
}

$allowedOrigin = 'https://www.example.com';
$origin = $_SERVER['HTTP_ORIGIN'] ?? '';

if ($origin !== '' && $origin !== $allowedOrigin) {
    http_response_code(403);
    echo json_encode(['ok' => false, 'message' => 'Request rejected']);
    exit;
}

$raw = file_get_contents('php://input');
if ($raw === false || strlen($raw) > 20000) {
    http_response_code(413);
    echo json_encode(['ok' => false, 'message' => 'Invalid request']);
    exit;
}

$data = json_decode($raw, true);
if (!is_array($data)) {
    http_response_code(400);
    echo json_encode(['ok' => false, 'message' => 'Invalid request']);
    exit;
}

$name = trim((string)($data['name'] ?? ''));
$email = trim((string)($data['email'] ?? ''));
$message = trim((string)($data['message'] ?? ''));
$honeypot = trim((string)($data['website'] ?? ''));

if ($honeypot !== '') {
    echo json_encode(['ok' => true]);
    exit;
}

if (
    mb_strlen($name) < 2 ||
    mb_strlen($name) > 80 ||
    !filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL) ||
    mb_strlen($message) > 1500
) {
    http_response_code(422);
    echo json_encode(['ok' => false, 'message' => 'Please check your details']);
    exit;
}

// Send through a configured SMTP library or trusted relay here.
// Do not concatenate unescaped values into email headers.

echo json_encode(['ok' => true, 'message' => 'Enquiry received']);
```

### Privacy requirements

- Tell users what their data will be used for.
- Request only necessary information.
- Do not preselect marketing consent.
- Add a privacy policy if forms collect personal details.
- Define a reasonable retention period.
- Give users a direct contact channel for deletion or correction requests.

---

## 14. GoDaddy `.htaccess`

Place this file in `public_html/.htaccess` after adapting the CSP domains.

```apacheconf
Options -Indexes

<IfModule mod_rewrite.c>
  RewriteEngine On

  # Redirect HTTP to HTTPS. Enable after SSL works correctly.
  RewriteCond %{HTTPS} !=on
  RewriteRule ^ https://%{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} [L,R=301]

  # Preserve real files, directories and optional PHP endpoints.
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} -f [OR]
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} -d
  RewriteRule ^ - [L]

  # React Router fallback.
  RewriteRule ^ index.html [L]
</IfModule>

<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
  Header always set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
  Header always set X-Frame-Options "DENY"
  Header always set Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()"
  Header always set Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin"

  # Adapt connect-src, img-src and frame-src before enabling third-party tools.
  Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: https:; media-src 'self' https:; connect-src 'self'; frame-src 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests"

  # Enable only after the HTTPS site is stable.
  Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
</IfModule>

<IfModule mod_expires.c>
  ExpiresActive On

  ExpiresByType text/html "access plus 0 seconds"
  ExpiresByType text/css "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType application/javascript "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/avif "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/webp "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/svg+xml "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType font/woff2 "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType video/mp4 "access plus 1 month"
</IfModule>

<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  <FilesMatch "\.(css|js|avif|webp|svg|woff2)$">
    Header set Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
  </FilesMatch>

  <FilesMatch "\.(html)$">
    Header set Cache-Control "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate"
  </FilesMatch>
</IfModule>

<FilesMatch "(^\.|\.env|package(-lock)?\.json|tsconfig.*\.json|vite\.config\..*)$">
  Require all denied
</FilesMatch>
```

### Important CSP note

The CSP above intentionally blocks Google Maps embeds, analytics and remote fonts. Add only the exact required origins after deciding which services will be used. Do not replace the policy with broad `*` permissions.

### React Router fallback warning

The fallback allows direct requests such as `/menu/` to return `index.html`. Real static files and directories are served normally. Keep `/api/` as a real directory so PHP requests are not rewritten.

---

## 15. Performance Strategy

The restaurant experience will be image-heavy, so performance discipline matters more than adding extra animation.

### Performance targets

Use these as project targets, not marketing guarantees:

- LCP at or below 2.5 seconds at the 75th percentile
- INP at or below 200 milliseconds at the 75th percentile
- CLS at or below 0.1 at the 75th percentile
- Initial mobile JavaScript kept as small as practical
- No unnecessary network requests before first render
- No layout shifts caused by images, fonts or utility-bar content

### Image rules

- Produce AVIF and WebP variants during development.
- Keep original high-resolution source files outside the deployed folder.
- Use responsive `srcset` and `sizes`.
- Always provide `width` and `height` or an explicit aspect ratio.
- Do not lazy-load the LCP hero image.
- Add `fetchpriority="high"` to the actual LCP image when appropriate.
- Lazy-load below-the-fold images.
- Use a poster image for every video.
- Avoid PNG for full-bleed photography.
- Do not ship 4000-pixel images to mobile users.

### Responsive image component

```tsx
interface ResponsiveImageProps {
  src: string;
  alt: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  sizes: string;
  priority?: boolean;
  className?: string;
}

export function ResponsiveImage({
  src,
  alt,
  width,
  height,
  sizes,
  priority = false,
  className,
}: ResponsiveImageProps) {
  return (
    <picture>
      <source type="image/avif" srcSet={`${src}-640.avif 640w, ${src}-1280.avif 1280w, ${src}-1920.avif 1920w`} />
      <source type="image/webp" srcSet={`${src}-640.webp 640w, ${src}-1280.webp 1280w, ${src}-1920.webp 1920w`} />
      <img
        src={`${src}-1280.webp`}
        alt={alt}
        width={width}
        height={height}
        sizes={sizes}
        loading={priority ? "eager" : "lazy"}
        fetchPriority={priority ? "high" : "auto"}
        decoding="async"
        className={className}
      />
    </picture>
  );
}
```

### Video rules

- Use video only when it improves the restaurant story.
- Compress to a practical bitrate and resolution.
- Keep mobile alternatives lighter.
- Use `muted`, `playsInline` and a poster for ambient autoplay video.
- Never autoplay sound.
- Pause videos outside the viewport when possible.
- Disable ambient autoplay for reduced-motion users.
- Do not delay the website behind a full video preload.

### JavaScript rules

- Lazy-load pages.
- Lazy-load heavy galleries or dialogs when opened.
- Use CSS instead of JavaScript for simple effects.
- Avoid importing the full icon collection.
- Import GSAP only where needed, or keep its use limited to a few sections.
- Do not attach global scroll listeners from individual cards.
- Use passive event listeners where appropriate.
- Avoid expensive state updates on every scroll frame.

### CSS rules

- Prefer transforms and opacity for motion.
- Avoid animating `width`, `height`, `top` and `left` during scroll.
- Avoid large animated blurs and shadows.
- Use `content-visibility: auto` carefully for very long below-fold sections.
- Do not apply `will-change` permanently to many elements.
- Reserve dimensions for dynamic content.

---

## 16. Accessibility Standard

Target **WCAG 2.2 Level AA** for the public experience.

### Global requirements

- Provide a skip link.
- Use semantic landmarks: `header`, `nav`, `main`, `section`, `footer`.
- Maintain a logical heading hierarchy.
- Ensure keyboard access for all controls.
- Show visible focus states.
- Ensure touch targets are reasonably large.
- Meet text and interactive contrast requirements.
- Never communicate state using colour alone.
- Use actual buttons for actions and anchors for navigation.
- Announce meaningful form errors.
- Move focus into dialogs and restore it on close.
- Allow Escape to close menus and dialogs.
- Lock background interaction when modal navigation is open.
- Avoid autoplaying carousels, or provide pause controls.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences.
- Provide captions or transcripts for meaningful spoken video.
- Ensure maps have a text address and directions link alternative.

### Mobile menu requirements

- Menu trigger has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
- Opening moves focus predictably.
- Tab focus remains within a modal-style full-screen menu.
- Escape closes it.
- Closing restores focus to the trigger.
- Background content cannot be operated while it is open.

### Form requirements

- Every input has a visible label.
- Required fields are indicated in text, not colour alone.
- Errors are associated through `aria-describedby`.
- Preserve entered values after validation failure.
- Use appropriate `autocomplete` tokens.
- Use `inputMode` for phone and numeric inputs.
- Disable the submit button only during a real submission.
- Provide a clear success state without immediately removing the user’s context.

---

## 17. Section-by-Section UX and Development Rules

## Home

### Hero

**Purpose:** Establish Amani’s atmosphere and drive reservations or menu exploration.

- One strong H1.
- One supporting paragraph.
- One primary CTA and at most one secondary CTA.
- Full-bleed media must not reduce text readability.
- Avoid generic phrases such as “Welcome to Amani” as the main headline.
- Show practical context such as cuisine, area or experience naturally.

### Mood Finder

**Purpose:** Help undecided users find a suitable dish or experience.

- Keep to a small number of meaningful choices.
- Show results immediately.
- Provide a direct path into Menu.
- Do not imitate a long personality quiz.

### Signature Experiences

**Purpose:** Explain why dining at Amani is distinctive.

- Use 2–4 strong experiences.
- Pair each with evidence, imagery or a specific benefit.
- Avoid generic icon cards.

### Signature Dishes

**Purpose:** Build appetite and reduce menu uncertainty.

- Show the dish name, short description, dietary marker and realistic price where approved.
- Include allergens when relevant.
- Link to the appropriate menu category or dish detail.

### The Amani Way

**Purpose:** Communicate philosophy through sourcing, cooking and hospitality.

- Use proof rather than vague claims.
- Do not overstate sustainability, locality or authenticity without evidence.

### Inside Amani

**Purpose:** Show real ambience and space.

- Use authentic photography.
- Keep alt text descriptive.
- Avoid stock imagery that misrepresents the venue.

### Guest Reviews

**Purpose:** Build trust.

- Publish genuine, approved testimonials.
- Identify the source only when permitted.
- Do not include structured aggregate ratings unless accurate and visibly supported.

### Visit Preview

- Show area, hours and directions.
- Provide a clear Visit link.

### Gatherings Preview

- Mention event types, approximate group suitability and enquiry path.
- Avoid promising capacity or services that are not confirmed.

## Stories

- Treat the page as editorial content, not a list of marketing cards.
- Use meaningful dates and real names where permitted.
- Keep long-form content readable.
- Add internal links back to Menu, Gatherings and Visit at natural points.
- Use progressive media loading.
- End with one clear action.

## Menu

- Use HTML menu content.
- Keep category navigation sticky with CSS.
- Support direct anchors such as `/menu/#mains`.
- Use stable dish IDs.
- Keep dietary icons understandable with labels or accessible text.
- Do not hide prices behind interaction.
- A dish dialog must use proper focus management.
- QR ordering must explain what the QR action does and offer a normal link alternative.
- Avoid auto-opening the camera from the website.

## Gatherings

- Clearly describe supported occasions.
- Display authentic venue photographs.
- Explain the enquiry process in a small number of steps.
- Set response-time expectations honestly.
- Keep the form concise.
- Confirm submission without exposing internal email details.

## Visit

- Put hours, address, directions, phone and reservation actions near the top.
- Calculate open/closed status using restaurant timezone.
- Show special-hour caveats.
- Include an accessible map alternative.
- Use clickable `tel:` and directions links.
- FAQs should answer real friction points: parking, accessibility, dietary requests, children, reservations, cancellation and large groups.

---

## 18. Error Handling and Resilience

### Route error boundary

- Show a calm branded error message.
- Provide Home, Menu and Contact options.
- Log technical details only in development or an approved monitoring tool.
- Never display stack traces in production.

### Asset failure

- Do not allow a broken hero image to leave unreadable text.
- Use background colours and aspect-ratio placeholders.
- Provide a poster fallback for video.

### Form failure

- Preserve entered information.
- Show a useful retry action.
- Offer direct phone or email contact.
- Avoid claiming success before the server confirms it.

### Offline/poor network

The first version does not need a complex PWA. The static site should still degrade gracefully through:

- small critical bundles
- cached hashed assets
- clear loading states
- no dependency on unnecessary API calls
- normal HTML links for contact and directions

---

## 19. Testing Strategy

### Required automated tests

#### Unit tests

- opening-hours calculations
- currency and date formatting
- URL creation
- form schema validation
- menu filtering

#### Component tests

- utility bar status states
- mobile menu open/close behavior
- form error associations
- dish dialog keyboard behavior
- FAQ interactions

#### Playwright user journeys

1. Open Home and navigate to Menu.
2. Directly load `/menu/` from a fresh browser session.
3. Open and close the mobile menu using keyboard controls.
4. Navigate to Gatherings and submit invalid form data.
5. Submit a valid mocked enquiry.
6. Open Visit and use directions and phone links.
7. Verify the 404 page.
8. Test reduced-motion behavior.

### Manual device matrix

- Android Chrome on an average device
- iPhone Safari
- Desktop Chrome
- Desktop Safari when available
- Firefox
- Keyboard-only navigation
- Screen reader smoke test
- 320–375px mobile width
- Tablet portrait and landscape
- Large desktop

### Quality tools

- Lighthouse
- Chrome Performance panel
- PageSpeed Insights after deployment
- axe or equivalent accessibility scanner
- Google Rich Results Test
- Search Console URL Inspection
- W3C HTML validation where useful

Automated scores do not replace manual UX and accessibility testing.

## 20. Code Quality Rules

### TypeScript

- Keep `strict` mode enabled.
- Avoid `any`.
- Validate external data at boundaries.
- Use discriminated unions for UI states when useful.
- Prefer explicit component props.

### React

- Keep rendering pure.
- Do not store derived values in state.
- Do not use effects for simple calculations.
- Clean up observers, timers, listeners and animations.
- Use stable keys from data, never array indexes for changing lists.
- Memoize only after measuring a reason.
- Avoid premature generic abstractions.

### Styling

- Use design tokens.
- Keep responsive rules consistent.
- Avoid arbitrary values when a token exists.
- Keep z-index values documented.
- Do not fix layout bugs with random negative margins.
- Ensure `overflow-x` is not being hidden merely to conceal broken layout.

### Git

- Use one focused branch per feature.
- Keep commits meaningful.
- Never commit `.env` secrets.
- Review generated build changes before upload.
- Tag stable releases.

### Pull-request checklist

- Scope is limited and clear.
- Existing content and functionality are preserved unless intentionally changed.
- Mobile behavior is tested.
- Keyboard behavior is tested.
- Reduced motion is tested.
- No console errors or warnings.
- No broken URLs or assets.
- Production build succeeds.
- Bundle impact is understood.
- SEO metadata is present.
- New external domains are reflected in CSP.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "tsc -b && vite build",
    "build:seo": "npm run build && node scripts/prerender.mjs",
    "preview": "vite preview",
    "lint": "eslint .",
    "format": "prettier --write .",
    "format:check": "prettier --check .",
    "test": "vitest run",
    "test:watch": "vitest",
    "test:e2e": "playwright test",
    "check": "npm run lint && npm run test && npm run build"
  }
}
```

Use `build:seo` only after the prerender script is implemented and tested.

## 22. Vite Configuration

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
  base: "/",
  build: {
    target: "es2020",
    sourcemap: false,
    cssCodeSplit: true,
    rollupOptions: {
      output: {
        manualChunks: {
          react: ["react", "react-dom", "react-router-dom"],
          motion: ["motion"],
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

### Configuration notes

- Keep `base: "/"` when deployed at the root domain.
- For a subfolder such as `example.com/amani/`, set `base: "/amani/"` and update router behavior and canonical URLs.
- Do not add manual chunks without checking the actual bundle; the example is a starting point.
- Do not ship production source maps publicly unless there is a clear monitoring requirement.

## 23. GoDaddy Deployment Process

### Local release commands

```bash
npm ci
npm run check
npm run build
```

The deployable website will be inside:

```text
dist/
```

### cPanel deployment

1. Open the GoDaddy hosting dashboard.
2. Open cPanel File Manager.
3. Go to the primary domain’s `public_html/` directory.
4. Back up the current website.
5. Remove obsolete hashed assets from the prior build.
6. Upload the **contents** of `dist/`, not the parent `dist` folder itself.
7. Upload the production `.htaccess` into `public_html/`.
8. Confirm SSL and HTTPS redirect behavior.
9. Test all direct URLs in a private browser window.
10. Verify form delivery, phone links, WhatsApp, directions and reservation actions.

### Critical post-deployment tests

Open these directly, not only through navigation:

```text
https://www.example.com/
https://www.example.com/stories/
https://www.example.com/menu/
https://www.example.com/gatherings/
https://www.example.com/visit/
https://www.example.com/not-a-real-page
```

Also verify:

- no mixed-content warnings
- no CSP errors blocking required resources
- no missing fonts
- no 404 errors for JavaScript or images
- correct canonical domain
- correct sitemap and robots URLs
- correct Open Graph preview
- enquiry submission
- mobile navigation

## 24. Maintenance Workflow

### Editing content

1. Update the relevant file in `src/content/` or `src/config/`.
2. Optimize any new images.
3. Run tests and build.
4. Upload the new `dist/` contents.
5. Recheck the changed page.

### Monthly checks

- Opening hours and special dates
- Menu availability and prices
- Reservation and directions links
- Broken links
- Enquiry delivery
- Search Console coverage
- Core Web Vitals
- Dependency security review
- Backup health

### Before a major campaign or festival

- Update special opening hours.
- Check reservation capacity wording.
- Prepare campaign social preview imagery.
- Test the site on mobile data.
- Avoid adding unoptimized temporary banners.
- Remove expired campaign content afterward.

- Semantic HTML and responsive CSS
- Tailwind design-system usage

### Skill boundary

A person who can create visually impressive animation but cannot handle cleanup, performance, accessibility, route loading and responsive behavior is not ready to own the production motion layer.

## 26. Development Methodology

Use the following sequence for every page and section.

### Phase 1 — Understand

- Confirm the user goal.
- Confirm the section’s primary CTA.
- Confirm the approved content and assets.
- Identify mobile constraints.
- Identify whether animation is necessary.

### Phase 2 — Static UX

- Build semantic markup.
- Establish hierarchy and spacing.
- Make it fully responsive.
- Ensure content works without motion.

### Phase 3 — Interaction

- Add keyboard and focus behavior.
- Add loading, error and empty states.
- Validate links and forms.

### Phase 4 — Motion

- Choose one animation owner.
- Add the signature effect.
- Add only essential supporting micro-interactions.
- Create reduced-motion and mobile alternatives.

### Phase 5 — Optimization

- Optimize images and video.
- Lazy-load routes and noncritical media.
- Profile the effect on a normal mobile device.
- Remove unnecessary work.

### Phase 6 — Verification

- Run lint, tests and production build.
- Test direct route loading.
- Test keyboard and reduced motion.
- Test on GoDaddy after deployment.

## 27. Definition of Done

A section is complete only when all relevant items pass.

### UX

- [ ] The section has one clear purpose.
- [ ] The main action is obvious.
- [ ] Content hierarchy is easy to scan.
- [ ] Mobile layout is intentionally designed.

### Visual design

- [ ] Matches the Amani design tokens.
- [ ] Feels minimal, warm and premium.
- [ ] Does not look like a generic SaaS component.
- [ ] Uses authentic imagery.

### Motion

- [ ] Motion supports the content.
- [ ] One library owns each property.
- [ ] GSAP effects clean up correctly.
- [ ] Mobile and reduced-motion variants exist.
- [ ] No scroll jank or unexpected pinning.

### Accessibility

- [ ] Correct semantic elements.
- [ ] Keyboard support.
- [ ] Visible focus.
- [ ] Meaningful alt text.
- [ ] Sufficient contrast.
- [ ] Form and dialog semantics pass.

### Performance

- [ ] Media dimensions are reserved.
- [ ] LCP media is prioritized.
- [ ] Below-fold media is lazy-loaded.
- [ ] No unnecessary dependencies were added.
- [ ] No console errors.

### SEO

- [ ] Unique title and description.
- [ ] Canonical URL.
- [ ] Crawlable links and content.
- [ ] Appropriate structured data.
- [ ] Sitemap includes the page.
- [ ] Prerendered output is checked when enabled.

### Security

- [ ] No secrets in the browser bundle.
- [ ] External domains are reviewed.
- [ ] CSP remains restrictive.
- [ ] Form data is validated server-side.
- [ ] No unsafe untrusted HTML rendering.

### Delivery

- [ ] Lint passes.
- [ ] Tests pass.
- [ ] Production build passes.
- [ ] Direct URL works on GoDaddy.
- [ ] Existing pages remain unaffected.

## 28. Prompt Template for Claude, Codex or Another Coding Agent

```text
Use the Amani Vite React Architecture document as the mandatory engineering standard.

Implement only the [PAGE / SECTION NAME] in the existing Amani restaurant project.

Goal:
[Explain what the section must communicate and the main user action.]

Preserve:
- all working routes, data and interactions
- the existing visual identity and content unless a change is explicitly requested
- all sections outside the requested scope
- the existing deployment compatibility with GoDaddy cPanel static hosting

Architecture constraints:
- React + Vite + TypeScript only for the main application
- no Node production server, Next.js, CMS, database, Docker or new backend framework
- use local typed content/configuration
- use the existing shared layout and components
- do not add dependencies without a clear need

Design direction:
- minimal, warm, editorial and luxurious restaurant presentation
- spacious hierarchy, authentic media and restrained details
- no generic SaaS cards, neon gradients, excessive pills, glassmorphism or decorative clutter

Motion rules:
- CSS for basic transitions
- Motion for React for component entrances, hover, presence and layout
- GSAP only for complex coordinated timelines
- ScrollTrigger only for genuine scroll-linked storytelling
- Lenis only as the single global smooth-scroll system
- never let two libraries animate the same property on the same element
- provide mobile and prefers-reduced-motion alternatives
- clean up all timelines, triggers, listeners and observers

Engineering requirements:
1. Inspect the existing repository before editing.
2. Build the static responsive layout before animation.
3. Use semantic HTML and WCAG 2.2 AA behavior.
4. Keep images responsive and reserve their dimensions.
5. Preserve crawlable text and normal anchor links.
6. Add or update route metadata and structured data where relevant.
7. Do not expose secrets in VITE_ variables.
8. Keep forms secure and validate again at the server endpoint.
9. Prevent horizontal overflow at 320px and 375px.
10. Run lint, tests and the production build.
11. Test direct route loading with the SPA fallback.
12. Implement the working code rather than only describing it.

Report after completion:
- files changed
- architecture decisions
- animation owner for each effect
- accessibility behavior
- mobile and reduced-motion behavior
- SEO impact
- performance impact
- checks run and results
```

## 29. Final Architecture Summary

The final production system should remain deliberately simple:

```text
React + TypeScript
        ↓
Vite production build
        ↓
Static dist/ files
        ↓
GoDaddy public_html
```

Supporting capabilities:

```text
React Router       → five public routes
Tailwind CSS       → design system and responsive layout
Motion for React   → interface and entrance motion
GSAP/ScrollTrigger → selected cinematic sections only
Lenis              → one global smooth-scroll layer
Local TS content   → menu and restaurant content
PHP/external form  → secure enquiry delivery only when needed
.htaccess          → HTTPS, route fallback, headers and caching
```

This approach offers the visual freedom needed for a refined restaurant experience while keeping deployment, ownership and maintenance practical for ordinary GoDaddy shared hosting.
